./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:7:Proofbound records several gate-consumed bindings against the current whole-tree
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:8:`materialHash`. That is sound, but too coarse for parallel story work: merging
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:9:an unrelated change into `main` can change the whole-tree hash and stale a
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:10:review run, verification evidence, or review escalation record even when the
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:11:story-owned files that record was actually attesting did not change.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:13:The fix is not to remove `materialHash`. Whole-tree drift can still represent
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:14:transitive dependency changes, runtime policy changes, or gate-fact changes that
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:15:are outside a story's direct file diff. The fix is to add a second, narrower
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:16:binding signal and make the downgrade explicit.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:20:Add `storyFilesHash` as an optional secondary freshness signal recorded
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:21:alongside, never instead of, the existing whole-tree `materialHash`.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:23:`storyFilesHash` is a deterministic SHA-256 over the story-owned material files:
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:25:1. Resolve the story's signed git workspace.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:26:2. Resolve the merge-base between current `HEAD` and `main`.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:27:3. Use the story's changed files between that merge-base and `HEAD`.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:28:4. Exclude story metadata and runtime artifacts with the same material-exclusion
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:29:   policy used by `materialHash`.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:30:5. Hash each remaining path with its blob object id at the target ref, sorted by
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:31:   path. Deleted story-owned paths are included with a deletion marker so
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:32:   removing a story-owned file changes the hash.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:34:The existing whole-tree `materialHash` remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:35:still recorded on every adopted binding. Consumers must not infer that a record
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:36:is fully fresh merely because `storyFilesHash` matches.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:40:The secondary signal applies to gate-consumed records whose validity is
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:41:currently evaluated through `materialHash` freshness:
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:43:- review runs and their workspace binding;
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:44:- checklist verification evidence;
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:45:- review escalation host verdicts and degraded fallback records.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:47:Legacy records without `storyFilesHash` keep the existing strict
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:48:`materialHash` behavior. Missing or uncomputable `storyFilesHash` must never
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:49:turn a stale `materialHash` record into a pass.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:53:When both a record and the current workspace have `storyFilesHash` values:
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:55:- matching `materialHash` means the record is fresh with no advisory;
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:56:- mismatching `materialHash` plus matching `storyFilesHash` means the record is
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:57:  valid for the story-owned file set, but the result must include an explicit
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:58:  whole-tree drift warning requiring re-attestation review;
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:59:- mismatching `storyFilesHash` means the record is stale and must be rejected;
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:60:- missing current `storyFilesHash` falls back to strict `materialHash` behavior.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:62:The warning is mandatory. This is not a silent rebind, not an automatic evidence
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:63:refresh, and not permission to rewrite stored hashes. Operators and reviewers
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:64:must see that unrelated whole-tree material drift occurred.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:66:## Why Not Story-Diff Only
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:68:Story-diff-only freshness is insufficient because Proofbound gates also depend on
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:69:shared runtime code and process facts. A story can leave its own changed files
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:70:untouched while a merge to `main` changes a transitive helper, validation
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:71:runner, review policy, or process-fact registry entry. Treating that as fully
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:72:fresh would hide a real risk. `storyFilesHash` therefore only downgrades the
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:73:failure from "reject as stale" to "valid with re-attestation advisory" when the
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:74:story-owned files did not change.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:76:## Rejected Alternatives
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:78:- Replace `materialHash` with story-diff-only hashing. Rejected because it hides
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:79:  transitive dependency and global gate-fact drift.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:80:- Silently rebind records to the current whole-tree hash when the story file set
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:81:  matches. Rejected because it erases audit history and makes stale evidence
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:82:  appear freshly attested.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:83:- Treat all whole-tree drift as fatal forever. Rejected because it blocks
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:84:  independent story work after unrelated `main` merges.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:88:`storyFilesHash` freshness is a gate-consumed process fact. The runtime
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:89:semantics must be registered in `process-fact-levels.ts`,
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:90:`process-fact-registry.ts`, and the process-fact contract verifier. The
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:91:registered semantics must state that story-owned file changes still invalidate
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:92:the binding, while unrelated whole-tree `materialHash` drift is only accepted
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:93:with an explicit re-attestation advisory.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:95:## DONE Sub-Gate Bindings (Amendment 2026-06-24)
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:97:The DONE gate has three freshness sub-gates. After review they are bound as follows.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:99:Adopted with extra guard (signed): delivery-check (core/delivery-check-hash.ts), the lattice-review-delivery reviewer's signed attestation of the story's git diff vs main, doc-promises, and real-machine tests. storyFilesHash is folded INTO the signed payload (signDeliveryCheck / recomputeDeliveryCheckHash) and persisted on the record; keying a relaxation on an unsigned field of a signed record is forbidden because it is forgeable. With storyFilesHash signed, materialHash mismatch + matching signed storyFilesHash downgrades to a mandatory re-attestation advisory (code delivery_check_drift_advisory), never to "fresh"; storyFilesHash mismatch hard-rejects; missing storyFilesHash falls back to strict; the stored hash is never rebound. Because delivery-check attests whole-tree behavioral claims (real-machine tests) and is the last gate before merge, the advisory must be operator-visible and direct re-attestation if the integrated runtime context changed.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:101:Kept strict (re-runs): the done-required build+full-test-suite evidence (core/done-required-validation.ts evaluateDoneRequiredEvidence). On whole-tree materialHash drift it re-runs the suite on the merged tree rather than downgrading, so behavioral breakage from an unrelated merge is caught directly; this cheap genuine re-verification is preferred over an advisory for the suite.
./docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md:103:Excluded (kept strict): the completed-DONE-projection evidence snapshot check (core/done-oracle.ts checkCompletedEvidenceSnapshotFreshness). It recomputes materialHash AT the recorded evidence.headHash (a frozen past ref) to verify the recorded (headHash, materialHash) pair is self-consistent — an evidence-integrity / tamper check, not a HEAD-drift freshness check. storyFilesHash computed at the same frozen ref yields no independent signal and an unrelated main merge does not change the tree at the recorded head, so this gate cannot exhibit the whole-tree-drift symptom; storyFilesHash MUST NOT be wired into it.

./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1240:## 9. Freshness, temporal binding, and drift
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1242:The new checks must reuse the canonical freshness reader and
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1243:`storyFilesHash` policy. They must not invent a second hash classifier.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1247:1. `storyFilesHash` drift is a strong signal that Story-owned material changed;
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1248:   topology evidence for affected claims is stale and must be re-run or
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1249:   independently re-attested according to the consuming gate.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1250:2. `closureFilesHash` drift is a strong signal that a discovered producer or
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1251:   consumer changed, including outside Story scope. The basis and affected
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1252:   evidence must be recomputed; a stable `storyFilesHash` is insufficient.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1253:3. `materialHash`-only drift with unchanged signed `storyFilesHash` and
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1254:   `closureFilesHash` is classified
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1255:   by the existing freshness policy. A permitted re-attestation remains explicit
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1256:   and auditable; it is never a silent pass.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1257:4. Legacy evidence without `storyFilesHash` follows the existing strict fallback.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1258:   It stays readable but cannot be upgraded to strong proof merely by rewriting
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1259:   metadata.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1260:5. `headHash` movement alone is not self-classified by the host. The canonical
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1261:   reader decides whether it is metadata/provenance movement or material drift.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1262:6. Temporal claims declare a cutoff policy. Producer assembly and verifier
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1263:   recomputation must consume the same immutable cutoff fact.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1264:7. Equality boundaries are explicit. If the policy says events at or after the
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1265:   cutoff are excluded, both `>` and `>=` mutations must be covered.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1266:8. Freshness repair must preserve original issuer, command, outcome, and evidence
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1267:   identity; otherwise it is a new run, not a refresh.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1268:9. Coverage-basis freshness is stricter than evidence freshness: a change to
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1269:   frozen scope, relevant diff hunks, registered producer/consumer facts,
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1270:   topology, frozen planned-path declaration, or discovery inputs requires basis
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1271:   recomputation. Rebinding an old path inventory or declaration projection to a
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1272:   new hash is forbidden.
./docs/requirements/decisions/proofstory-acceptance-topology-and-pre-review-gates-execution-plan.md:1274:## 10. Applicability and compatibility

./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:9:This document describes the formal proof-root invariant guard implemented for
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:10:Layer 2 Engineering and Layer 3 Loop Engineering baseline suite aggregation.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:12:The invariant prevents stale, mixed, local-only, wrong-target, or
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:13:authority-overclaim final-report artifacts from polluting a formal unlock proof
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:14:root.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:18:All changes in B-9d6c follow these four principles:
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:20:```text
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:21:Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:23:Only fix real correctness issues.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:24:Preserve consistency of logic.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:27:The invariant exists because mixed or stale artifacts in a formal proof root are
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:28:a real correctness issue: they can produce a false PASS suite report.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:32:The root invariant is applied during formal baseline suite aggregation for
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:33:`engineering` and `loop-engineering` layers. It inspects every parsed
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:34:`final-report.json` inside the selected layer root, not only reports that match
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:35:accepted baselines.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:37:A formal suite aggregation is BLOCKED when any parsed final report in the
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:38:selected root violates any of the following conditions:
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:40:| Condition | Required value | Violation meaning |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:42:| `layer` | Must match the expected layer (`engineering` or `loop-engineering`) | Mixed-layer artifact in the root |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:43:| `materialHash` | Must match the current material hash | Stale evidence state |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:44:| `suiteRunId` | Must be present and identical across all reports in the root | Mixed or missing suite run identity |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:45:| `claimTarget` | Must match the expected claim target (`engineering` or `loop-engineering`) | Wrong proof target |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:46:| `localOnly` | Must be `false` | Local-only artifact posture |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:47:| `capabilityProof` | Must be `true` | Non-proof artifact in proof root |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:48:| `formalProof` | Must be `true` | Non-formal artifact in formal root |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:49:| `falseDone` | Must be `false` | False DONE artifact |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:50:| `authority.authorityDone` | Must be `false` for Layer 2/3 CLI proof | Authority overclaim |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:51:| `authority.receiptVerified` | Must be `false` for Layer 2/3 CLI proof | Authority overclaim |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:52:| `authority.productionDone` | Must be `false` for Layer 2/3 CLI proof | Authority overclaim |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:53:| `authority.fullAuthorityDone` | Must be `false` for Layer 2/3 CLI proof | Authority overclaim |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:55:`headHash` remains a source binding on generated final reports and suite
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:56:reports, but it is not a current-HEAD root invariant. Formal proof artifacts may
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:57:be generated against a source HEAD and then committed as artifact material,
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:58:which legitimately changes git HEAD while preserving the same proof material
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:59:hash. The mechanical stale gate therefore uses `materialHash` plus stored-vs-
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:60:rebuilt accepted report bindings for this story.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:62:When the invariant blocks, the suite report emits explicit blocked reasons
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:63:naming the specific field and mismatch (e.g. `suiteRunId`, `claimTarget`,
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:64:`materialHash`, `localOnly`) so that auditors can distinguish failure modes.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:66:## 4. Stale-Trap Negative Root Separation
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:68:Stale-trap and negative-control artifacts (mixed `suiteRunId`, wrong
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:69:`claimTarget`, `localOnly=true`, Authority overclaim posture) must not exist
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:70:inside the selected formal PASS root. They belong in a separate negative-check
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:71:root used only by smoke tests and negative coverage.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:73:The separation is:
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:77:| Selected formal PASS root (e.g. `.lattice/artifacts/baseline/layer2-engineering-unlock`) | Formal proof aggregation | Only clean, current-run, single-`suiteRunId`, correct-`claimTarget` final reports |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:78:| Negative-check root (smoke test fixtures) | Prove fail-closed behavior | Stale `materialHash`, mixed `suiteRunId`, wrong `claimTarget`, `localOnly=true`, Authority overclaim artifacts |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:80:The root invariant scans only the selected formal PASS root. Negative-check
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:81:artifacts outside that root do not pollute formal suite aggregation. Historical
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:82:audit artifacts from previous runs also do not pollute the current formal root
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:83:as long as they are not placed inside the selected root directory.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:85:## 5. Layer 4 Production Safety Boundary
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:87:Layer 4 Production Safety remains a precondition-only consumer of the artifact
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:88:isolation invariant. The invariant implemented in B-9d6c does not unlock
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:89:Production Safety and does not enable any Production Safety claims.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:91:Layer 4 unlock requires capabilities that do not exist in this story:
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:93:| Missing capability | Why it matters |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:95:| Production-safety evaluator | A formal evaluator that can authorize `production-safety` claims does not exist. The current `capability_claim_evaluate` is L0/read-only diagnostic for Layer 2/3 only. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:96:| Authority proof chain | Production Safety requires real Authority Server receipts (`receiptVerified=true`, `productionDone=true`). Proofbound CLI cannot produce these. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:97:| Soak evidence | Production Safety baselines require `soak-summary.json` and `recovery-log.jsonl` from real sustained operation. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:98:| Multi-host authority verification | Production Safety requires verified independent multi-host proof, not just independent review verdicts. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:100:Until a production-safety evaluator and Authority-backed proof chain exist,
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:101:Layer 4 may only consume the artifact isolation invariant as a precondition
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:102:check. It cannot use the invariant to claim production readiness.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:104:The formal claim boundary after B-9d6c:
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:106:```text
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:107:Layer 2 Engineering Baseline    = can be formally unlocked (invariant guard active)
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:108:Layer 3 Loop Engineering        = can be formally unlocked (invariant guard active)
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:109:Layer 4 Production Safety       = LOCKED (no evaluator, no Authority proof chain)
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:113:## 6. What This Invariant Does Not Do
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:115:- Does not verify Authority Server receipts. Proofbound CLI remains non-authority.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:116:- Does not convert Claude or Codex host verdicts into Authority evidence.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:118:- Does not add new capability layers or broader runner rewrites.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:119:- Does not downgrade a blocked suite into PASS for momentum.
./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:120:- Does not treat local diagnostic artifacts as formal proof.

./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:128:## 8. Relation to Existing Decision Documents

./docs/requirements/decisions/formal-unlock-artifact-isolation-execution-plan.md:133:- `unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md` (Section 8: Evidence Contract, Section 12: Fail-Closed Rules)

./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:17:## Problem Statement
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:19:Proofbound already accumulates a large volume of structured data with outcomes:
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:20:findings and their final state, `checklist.json`, `decision.json`, story
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:21:background, and `activity.jsonl`. Today this data only
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:22:serves the current story; it is never reused across stories.
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:24:What makes Proofbound different from ordinary agent memory is that it knows, for
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:25:any given problem, which story it appeared in, how the reviewer judged it at the
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:26:time, whether it was finally resolved / dismissed / accepted-as-risk, whether it
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:27:passed the gate, and whether it caused rework or a rollback. That is verified,
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:28:outcome-bearing evidence, not a guess.
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:30:The Experience Layer turns this verified history into an auditable,
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:31:rollback-able, explainable layer of **review hints** and **process playbooks**.
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:32:It does not make any agent "smarter" on its own; it makes past, verified evidence
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:33:appear on time and auditably at the next review. The one-line positioning is:
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:35:> **Learning suggests. Human and gate decide.**
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:37:The core principle is unchanged from v1.0: Proofbound does not let an agent be
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:38:clever on its own; Proofbound lets evidence that has actually happened and has been
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-experience-layer-execution-plan.md:39:verified appear, on time and auditably, at the next review.

./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3158:### X8. Core AI Execution Principle: Anti-Over-Optimization Gate
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3160:This is a core AI execution principle for the whole development flow.
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3162:Whenever the AI proposes an optimization, refactor, abstraction, extra checklist
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3163:item, broader architecture change, or "nice to have" improvement, it must first
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3164:challenge its own suggestion. The planner, executor, provider prompt, and
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3165:reviewers must repeatedly ask whether the proposed change is required for the
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3166:requested outcome. This is a lightweight self-questioning gate, not a new
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3171:```text
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3172:Is this change necessary to satisfy the user request, lifecycle gate,
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3173:verification intent, evidence requirement, or safety policy?
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:3176:If the answer is no, the change is deferred.

./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4479:| Runner liveness is mistaken for authority approval. | DONE requires native `gate_decision` receipt. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4480:| Provider output prose is mistaken for evidence. | Only structured evidence and verified receipts satisfy gates. |

./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4483:| Dirty user work is overwritten. | Worktree scope checks and before/after git evidence. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4484:| Bootstrap token becomes too powerful. | It only authorizes actor key registration. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4485:| Key discovery is spoofed in production. | HTTPS/tunnel plus key pinning. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4486:| Non-authority mode contacts the server. | Local/non-authority mode never reads `authority.md` or calls Authority endpoints. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4487:| Default localhost Authority weakens production. | `http://localhost:6789/` is a local authority development default only; production must be explicit and pinned. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4488:| Default test key is used for production DONE. | Default test keys and `local-test` profiles are rejected outside deterministic tests/local development. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4489:| `authority.md` leaks private key material. | The file is internal, gitignored when private material is present, excluded from evidence, and overridden by explicit env/CLI config. |

requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4491:| Local autopilot regresses. | Local/shadow regression tests are mandatory in final matrix. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4492:| Interactive planner modes become untestable chat. | Structured answer/decision/resume commands are mandatory. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4493:| Autonomous/interview high-risk ambiguity silently hard-blocks. | Bounded 2-3 host decision waves may resolve policy-allowed ambiguity and resume; unresolved decisions stop blocked. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4494:| Multi-host verification is faked by duplicate sessions. | Independent host rules and verdict endpoints are mandatory. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4495:| Single-host fallback is mislabeled as full DONE. | Full authority DONE requires multi-host pass; single-host evidence is diagnostic only. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4496:| Local review is mislabeled as Authority DONE. | Local review sets only `localReviewCertified`; Authority flags remain false. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4497:| Old verifier verdicts pass after repair. | Repair that changes material state forces fresh anchors, fresh receipts when applicable, and a fresh review wave. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4498:| Verdict host identity is spoofed in JSON. | Authority derives host identity from authenticated actor/host/session/key binding. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4499:| Multi-host review becomes an expensive per-step loop. | Review waves run only at final certification or high-risk final gates. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4500:| Preferred Gemini verifier becomes a hard dependency. | Gemini is a preferred verifier host only when registered and policy requires or prefers it. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4501:| Agent count is optimized for its own sake. | Concurrency is bounded by milestone wave, non-overlapping write-set, Story readiness, and host independence; 13-15 agents is a temporary burst ceiling, not the default target. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4502:| Evidence storage grows without bound. | Retention classes and garbage collection rules are required. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4503:| Provider secrets leak into evidence. | Credential sourcing and redaction policy fail closed. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4504:| Per-run authority DONE is mislabeled as full DONE. | Final JSON separates `authorityDone` from `fullAuthorityDone` and reports multi-host fields. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4505:| Planner emits unsupported step types. | Job Planner fixtures prove B1 allowlist compatibility. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4506:| Evidence idempotency drops records. | Evidence idempotency key includes a per-record sequence or content digest. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4507:| Source-aligned redevelopment leaks source secrets or proprietary material. | Source is read-only, excluded paths are enforced, secrets are redacted/excluded, and evidence prefers digests/refs. |

./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4509:| Source-aligned redevelopment overclaims alignment. | DONE requires deterministic module/function alignment maps, rename-map evidence, build/test parity, and explicit gap records. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4510:| Cross-language redevelopment is marketed as exact semantic identity. | The contract is evidence-backed observable parity plus explicit gaps; Proofbound must not claim perfect equivalence for arbitrary language pairs. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4511:| A language pair becomes hardcoded special-case behavior. | `sourceLanguage -> targetLanguage` runs through language adapters, neutral manifests, semantic mapping policy, and target-runnable parity oracles. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4512:| Missing language adapters are hidden behind provider prose. | Missing adapters block or produce scoped gaps; provider output cannot replace deterministic manifest extraction. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4513:| Source-only tests burn budget in cross-language repair loops. | Untranslatable checks route directly to `gapList[]` or blocked stop reasons instead of repeated repair attempts. |
./docs/requirements/decisions/lattice-authority-live-integration.md:4514:| Source-aligned redevelopment loops on gaps. | Gap remediation consumes existing repair/no-progress counters plus redevelopment-specific caps and then blocks with `gapList[]`. |

./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:364:## Story Slicing Recommendation
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:366:Preferred split:
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:368:1. Story A: `done_prepare` post-validation progress and heartbeat.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:369:2. Story B: early review-assurance surfacing and blocker recipes.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:370:3. Story C: DONE merge-preflight and re-run delta UX.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:372:If these ship in one story, keep the scope UX-only: progress, status, guidance,
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:373:and tests. Do not change gate criteria or create new auto-attestation paths.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:378:- A later closeout idle/max timeout preserves any already-observed validation disposition, evidence basis, and refusal reasons; only the later terminal result/layer changes to `timed_out` and `idle|max`. The command-level `done_prepare` budget is the exact sum of routine validation plus each enabled closeout phase once (five non-validation phases, plus DONE-required only when enabled). CLI named deadline errors propagate through routine verifier execution so a command deadline that lands between watchdog polling ticks retains `timeoutLayer=max`.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:380:- Closeout segments check the parent watchdog before and after each segment and await cooperative abort cleanup. Synchronous JavaScript is inherently non-preemptible, so it stops at the first deadline/checkpoint boundary. Pure in-process closeout segments spawn no descendants, making process-tree ESRCH evidence not applicable there; descendant cleanup is required and tested only for validation/phase paths that actually spawn children.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:382:DONE-required execution and reuse use one bounded contract:
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:384:- The DONE-required phase budget is the safe sum of effective sequential command timeouts plus bounded grace. A phase-specific override wins the global phase override, which wins the derived budget. The direct `done_required_validate` CLI max covers that derived phase; the `done_prepare` CLI max covers routine validation plus every enabled closeout phase. An explicit `LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` remains authoritative. Each effective command timeout is capped at Node's maximum legal timer delay before arming the real timer, so a huge configured value cannot overflow into an immediate timeout. Structured `failed` / `timed_out` / `blocked` results remain parseable on stdout and exit nonzero; routine `done_prepare` idle/max aborts use the same terminal timeout shape and release child processes, timers, and locks for an immediate rerun.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:385:- `done_prepare` defaults `reuseFreshDoneRequired=true`, independently of post-closeout `reuseFreshValidation`. Reuse requires the canonical DONE-required evaluator to pass and evidence HEAD to equal current HEAD, or be its ancestor with every path touched by every intervening commit classified as trusted story metadata (including modify-then-revert history). HEAD must remain unchanged across evaluation. Any code, config, non-metadata, non-ancestor, unreadable evidence/lineage, or concurrent HEAD movement refuses reuse.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:386:- `validate:false` means `disposition=skipped_explicitly` and `result=not_run`; it neither executes nor reuses nor manufactures evidence, while reporting `existingEvidenceBasis=fresh|stale|missing`. Executed and reused paths report `disposition`, `result`, `refusalReasons`, and any `timeoutLayer` in human and JSON output.
./docs/requirements/decisions/done-prepare-heartbeat-review-assurance-ux-execution-plan.md:387:- Progress and heartbeat output uses stderr/the logging side channel, never JSON stdout. Reporter failures are diagnostic-only. Heartbeats refresh idle liveness only; command, phase, idle, and absolute max deadlines, child-tree termination, lock release, and timer cleanup remain independent.

./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:10:## 1. What a quorum asserts (and does not)
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:12:A valid Tier-C quorum asserts: **two verdicts, each Ed25519-signed by a distinct pinned host key,
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:13:each bound to the same materialHash, were produced by two different vendor hosts reviewing the same
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:14:code, and both pass — and any third party can verify this offline.**
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:16:It does NOT assert: that the two hosts are on different machines, different operators, or a
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:17:mutually-hostile trust boundary. See the independence ceiling (§3).
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:19:## 2. Trust anchor: the pinned key manifest
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:21:- Trust is anchored in a pinned `[hostId → publicKeyBase64]` manifest distributed **out-of-band**
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:22:  (committed to the repo / shipped with the verifier), never taken from the verdict body.
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:23:- A verdict's signer key is verified against the PINNED key for its claimed hostId, not the
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:24:  self-reported key in the bundle (mirrors the existing `receipt-bundle.ts` rule: verify against
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:25:  `context.publicKey`, never the bundle's own).
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:26:- Manifest is versioned; a verdict records the manifest version it was signed under.
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:28:## 3. Independence definition and its honest ceiling
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:30:- **Claimed independence = cross-vendor:** host A = Claude (Anthropic model family), host B = Codex
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:31:  (OpenAI model family) — distinct vendors, distinct model families, distinct signing keys held
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:32:  separately. This is the property the paper may claim.
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:33:- **Ceiling (must be stated, not hidden):** the two hosts are orchestrated by the SAME operator on
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:34:  (possibly) the same machine. So the guarantee is **cross-vendor independence of review**, NOT a
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:35:  sysadmin-level mutually-distrusting distributed-trust model. The paper's Threats section keeps:
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:36:  "cross-vendor independent, same-operator orchestrated; not a Byzantine multi-party trust claim."
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:37:- Consequence for wording (M5): allowed = "an independent second-vendor host produced a
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:38:  cryptographically verifiable verdict"; forbidden = "mutually-distrusting parties" / "no operator
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:41:## 4. Threats and fail-closed defenses (the rules M-crypto/M2 enforce)
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:43:| Threat | Attack | Defense (fail-closed) |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:45:| Forged verdict | unsigned, or signed by a non-pinned key | reject: signature must verify against the pinned key for that hostId |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:46:| Same-key masquerade | one CLI/key emits both "independent" verdicts | reject: quorum requires two DISTINCT pinned keys (this is the core M-crypto fix — until then independence is cross-vendor label-only, not key-enforced) |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:47:| Stale materialHash | a host reviewed old code, submits over a drifted tree | reject: materialHash freshness check + the M2 handshake (both hosts pinned to the same tree sha before either submits) |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:48:| Replay | reuse a previously-valid signed verdict | reject: verdict binds materialHash + round + timestamp; a verdict is admissible only for its bound (material, round) |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:49:| Partial/omission | drop one verdict, or `push(null)` after signing | reject: strict bundle-shape check (the F-005 anti-null-elision defense already in `receipt-bundle.ts`) |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:50:| Key compromise | a pinned private key leaks | rotate: manifest version bump + revocation list; verdicts under a revoked key are inadmissible from the revocation timestamp |
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:52:Global rule: on ANY of {signature invalid, key not pinned, two same keys, stale/missing materialHash,
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:53:missing signature, malformed bundle} the quorum does NOT form. There is no "soft" path — the fallback
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:54:is always full recompute / hard reject, never a relaxed accept (keeps Eq.adm un-weakened).
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:58:- **Generation:** each host generates its own Ed25519 keypair locally (`authority-signing.ts`
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:59:  `generateEd25519KeyPair`); private keys never leave the host.
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:60:- **Pinning/distribution:** public keys are added to the committed manifest by an explicit operator
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:61:  action (out-of-band), not auto-trusted on first use.
./docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md:62:- **Rotation:** manifest-versioned; a rotation adds the new key and marks the old one retired-at a

./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:200:### expect Matching Rules
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:202:1. **Partial match**: each field in expect must exist in actual and be equal; actual may have extra fields
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:203:2. **pattern regex**: if expect contains a `pattern` field, match actual with a regex (a string is matched directly, an object is JSON.stringify'd first)
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:204:3. **throws error match**: the throws field is a string, and it passes if the actual error message contains that string

./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:362:For each case in the fixture:
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:363:  1. If case.executor exists, select the corresponding executor
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:364:  2. Otherwise, if case.execute exists, fall back to js.execute
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:365:  3. Otherwise, if case.command exists, fall back to command
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:366:  4. The executor returns actual or throws
./docs/requirements/decisions/test-fixture-spec.md:367:  5. The runner uniformly judges with expect / throws and writes evidence / bug / gate

./docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:760:human UX for prompt-consolidation milestone tracking. Prompt status such as
./docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:761:`active`, `conditional`, `advisory`, `folded`, `retired`, `legacy`, or
./docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:762:`not_routed` is registry/routing metadata, not a milestone row state. The
./docs/requirements/decisions/proof-or-stop-agent-prompt-consolidation-execution-plan.md:763:user-visible progress UX must come from `lattice milestone_status`, not from

## Original Problem

Before the implemented main write lock and story owner lease rollout, Proofbound
supported parallel story worktrees but did not mechanically own write
coordination across sessions. The remaining B-a781 work is narrower: migrate
session identity resolution to the canonical host-adapter `LATTICE_SESSION_ID`
contract without regressing the implemented write-coordination baseline.

The rollout was designed to prevent these failure modes:

- Two sessions can mutate the same story metadata and confuse phase or evidence state.
- Two DONE flows can race on main and leave partial-DONE recovery work.
- Shared B-META writes such as `gap_log` can duplicate findings.
- Agents relying on human chat coordination instead of Proofbound-enforced ownership.

Proofbound must allow parallel work while making write authority explicit.

## Goals

1. Multiple stories may progress in parallel.
2. One story has one mutating owner session at a time.
3. Shared main and B-META writes are serialized.
4. Stale sessions can be recovered explicitly.
5. Read-only inspection is always allowed.
6. Errors and `session_brief` must tell agents whether to proceed, wait, or request takeover.

## Terms

- `sessionId`: stable identity for one agent session.
- `story owner lease`: exclusive right to run mutating commands for one story.
- `main write lock`: global lock for writes to main or shared metadata.
- `stale lease`: owner lease with heartbeat older than the configured threshold.
- `takeover`: explicit transfer of a story lease to another session.
- `read-only command`: command that does not mutate story, main, or B-META state.
- `mutating command`: command that writes story metadata, code, review evidence, findings, lifecycle state, or shared audit state.

## Command Classes

### Read-Only Commands

Always allowed. Examples:

- `session_brief`
- `story_get`
- `story_list`
- `checklist_get`
- `finding_list`
- `convergence_check`
- `doctor` read-only scans
- audit report reads

### Story-Scoped Mutating Commands

Require the story owner lease.

Examples:

- `story_advance`, except INIT_CHECK creation edge cases
- `checklist_update`
- `understanding_set`
- `decision_set`
- `finding_resolve` or `finding_dismiss` for a normal story
- `validate` when it writes evidence
- `delivery_check_set`
- `summary_set`

### ReviewerWrite Gate Evidence Commands

These commands write REVIEW evidence but are `reviewerWrite`, not story-owner
mutations. Per `packages/main/src/core/command-policy.ts`, `reviewerWrite` is
exempt from the owner lease; see `review-run-binding-race.md` for why owner-lease
serialization does not solve the review-run binding race.

Examples:

- `review_run_start`
- `review_pass_set`
- `finding_add` for a normal story

### Main/Shared Mutating Commands

Require the main write lock. Some also require a story owner lease.

Examples:

- `story_create`
- `story_advance DONE` merge and cleanup
- `done_recover`
- `gap_log`
- `audit --framework` when it writes reports or findings
- finding mutations on `B-META-framework-audit`
- commands that update main mirror metadata

### Dangerous Mutating Commands

Require the relevant lease plus explicit user or takeover intent.

Examples:

- force takeover of an active non-stale story
- discard another session's active story
- recovery commands that merge to main
- cleanup commands that remove worktrees or branches

## Story Owner Lease Rules

1. The first story-scoped mutating command for a story acquires the owner lease.
2. The lease records `sessionId`, hostname, pid, cwd, command, `acquiredAt`, `heartbeatAt`, and optional human label.
3. Owner commands refresh `heartbeatAt`.
4. Non-owner story-scoped mutating commands fail closed.
5. Read-only commands do not require a lease and do not refresh ownership.
6. Lease is released when the story reaches DONE or DISCARDED and cleanup succeeds.
7. Lease may be marked stale after 30 minutes without heartbeat.
8. A stale lease can be taken over with explicit `--takeover`, recording an event.
9. A non-stale lease requires explicit `--forceTakeover` and should be treated as human-approved.

## Main Write Lock Rules

1. Main/shared mutations must acquire a global mkdir-style lock.
2. The lock must be atomic and stale-reclaimable.
3. The lock scope must cover the whole critical section, not just the final write.
4. DONE must hold the main write lock from pre-merge final check through merge and worktree cleanup.
5. B-META finding writes must hold the main write lock and perform idempotency checks inside the lock.
6. Lock acquisition failure is blocking. Proofbound must not proceed optimistically.

## Storage

Preferred storage:

- story lease: `.lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/owner-lease.json`
- main write lock: `.lattice/locks/main-write.lock/`
- command event trail: existing process-events/activity stream

> Runtime note (B-f60c): `.lattice/locks/main-write.lock/` is the single canonical
> main write lock path. The former DONE-specific merge serialization lock
> `.lattice/runtime/done-main-merge.lock` has been retired with no back-compat
> alias — the DONE merge / `done_recover` critical sections now acquire the
> unified lock at the path above. `story-lifecycle.md` references the same
> canonical path; the two docs are synchronized.

The lease file is process metadata, not product evidence. It should be visible in `session_brief` but should not count as verification evidence.

Blocked rows are provider-honest: a refusal records the provider of the host
that was asked to run (`openai` for codex, `anthropic` for claude,
`antigravity` for agy), never a hard-coded default.

The autopilot Claude repair launch (`lattice autopilot execute
--allowClaudeRepair`) passes the **same pre-spawn admission** in both ledger
modes. With the ledger ON, budget and capacity refusals can also write the
diagnostic blocked row. With the ledger OFF there are no usage rows or budget
guard, but capacity admission remains mandatory and the slot is still released
after the run.

The `cross_host_review` Codex leaf runs through ManagedHostRun and the same
provider admission (provider `openai`). It supports detach/resume by exact
`managedRunId`, never spawns a replacement on resume, and binds the terminal
`receiptId` into host-B verdict provenance. Budget/cap/provider failures still
produce an honest blocked/error decision; raw stdout is never gate evidence.

Concurrent runs' ledger appends are serialized by a cross-process lock at the
writer choke point (an atomic `llm-usage.jsonl.lock/` directory with a bounded
wait), so parallel host runs can never interleave appends and break the ledger
hash chain — a writer that cannot acquire the lock in time skips its append
(an honest under-count) rather than corrupting the chain. Lock reclaim is
ownership-aware: the acquirer records `owner.json` (holder pid + a unique
release token) inside the lock dir, and a held lock is reclaimed only when
that pid is dead, or — for an ownerless/corrupt lock, i.e. the holder crashed
between creating the dir and recording ownership — when the dir mtime exceeds
the `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER_LOCK_STALE_MS` orphan backstop. A live holder is
never reclaimed no matter how long it holds the lock (slow filesystem, GC
pause, suspension); release removes the lock only while `owner.json` still
carries the releaser's own token.

There is **no queuing** in this story: over the cap means refuse, not wait.

Set `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0` to disable usage preflight/budget/final rows. It
does **not** disable ManagedHostRun ownership or provider-process admission.

## Diagnostics, cleanup, and trust boundary

`lattice doctor --full` lists every managed run with state, worker liveness,
worker heartbeat, provider progress mode/time, deadline, cancellation,
residual-process status, `replacementSafe`, and retention state. `lattice
doctor --repair` removes heavy terminal run directories only after the 90-day
retention window and first archives the sealed minimal receipt plus imported
evidence-binding digest under `.lattice/runtime/host-run-receipts/`. Active or
corrupt runs and any directory still carrying one-shot inputs are retained
fail-closed for inspection; failed launch/claim paths erase prompt, capability,
and one-shot environment immediately. The imported binding carries a separate
immutable digest seal, so a shape-preserving binding rewrite is corrupt before
doctor/GC can delete it. Expired cross-host runs also remove only their canonical
`lattice-xhr-review-*/worktree` snapshot; paths outside that tmp boundary fail
closed. Per-run live output is capped at 8 MiB;
status readers page bounded frames and surface truncation rather than loading an
unbounded transcript.

The runtime directory is local and mode 0700; sensitive one-shot files are 0600.
This protects against other users under ordinary filesystem permissions, not a
same-UID/root attacker. Operators must treat retained live output as locally
sensitive. Native Codex/Claude subagent APIs are deliberately out of scope:
ManagedHostRun owns only cross-provider CLI processes launched by Proofbound.

## `usage_sweep` (read-only retro-attribution)

```
lattice usage_sweep --since 2026-07-01 [--json]
```

`usage_sweep` stream-reads `~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl` and
`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` since a cutoff and reports per-session token
totals, originator (desktop vs exec vs claude-code), cwd, first/last timestamps,
and `B-xxxx` story mentions, plus a per-story rollup and grand totals. It exists
to make runs that never went through `host_run` (interactive desktop sessions in
particular) at least visible.

- The report header states **NON-AUTHORITATIVE ESTIMATE** prominently in both
  the human table and `--json`. The totals come from host transcript stores, not
  billing truth.
- It performs **no ledger backfill**: swept sessions are never written into the
  usage ledger.
- It is strictly **read-only**. The only write it can perform is an explicit
  `--out <path>` JSON report, and that write is create-only and fenced:
  - `--out` must be a **relative** path that resolves inside the project root;
    absolute paths and any `..` traversal escaping the root are refused
    outright.
  - It only ever **creates a new report file** — the file is opened with the
    exclusive-create `wx` flag, so an already-existing target is refused
    atomically and `usage_sweep` can never overwrite or truncate anything
    (not even via a symlink at the target path).
  - It refuses to write through **symlinked ancestor directories**, and the
    resolved real path must still fall inside the (realpath'd) project root,
    so an inside-root symlink cannot redirect the report outside the project.
  - Missing report directories are created only **after** all of those checks
    pass.

- Usage rows **never gate the workflow** — they are `gateEvidence=false`

- Interactive desktop host sessions are **out of reach** of the choke point;
  they are report-only via `usage_sweep`, never through `host_run`.
- `usage_sweep` never mutates story, ledger, or lifecycle state and never
  backfills the ledger.

Inside the provider process, the managed prompt forbids `review_run_start`,
`review_pass_set` and `finding_add`. Its final assistant result must be exactly
one bounded `lattice.managed_review_final_proposal.v1` JSON envelope containing
pass-or-findings plus truthful read evidence. After a successful provider exit,
the managed adapter selects only Codex's terminal `item.completed`
`agent_message` or Claude's terminal `result`; tool logs, arbitrary streamed
stdout and controller fields are ignored. The worker validates the sealed

Missing, malformed, multiple or oversized envelopes fail the run closed. The
older descriptor-authorized `managed_review_proposal_set` command remains a
compatibility path, not the formal happy path; its private signing key is never
placed in the prompt, argv, provider environment, or durable run artifact.
Raw same-UID CLI calls, copied environment variables, stale PGIDs,
terminal/reaped runs, and ambiguous/multiple run candidates fail closed.
Successful terminal creation seals the proposal and journal;
the importer accepts only `runId + receiptId`, exposes no verdict override, and
preserves the provider lane/ReviewRun/provenance. Both import time and the REVIEW
gate revalidate the same shared Proof Admissibility contract. Raw CLI stdout,
usage rows and time-window correlations cannot satisfy this evidence class.

`host_run_worker` is an internal continuation command. It remains dispatchable
by the detached launcher but is omitted from ordinary help/catalog discovery;
operators use `host_run`, `host_run_status`, and `host_run_cancel`.

## Binding conventions

Every usage row carries the attribution passed to `host_run`:

| Argument | Ledger field | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--storyId` | `storyId` | Canonical Story id. Omit for an adhoc run. |
| `--agentType` | `agentType` | e.g. `reviewer`, `autopilot-repair`, `host-readiness-probe`. Required. |
| `--phase` | `phase` | When omitted and `--storyId` is set, the phase resolves from the **configured story store** at call time (honoring a project's `storyDir`); an explicit `--phase` is used as-is and the store is never read. |
| `--reviewRunId` | `threadId` | e.g. `B-xxxx:RR-001`. Joins rows against `review-runs.json`. |
| `--lane` | `subagentId` | e.g. `lattice-review-quality`. |

`--reviewRunId` must start with `<storyId>:` when `--storyId` is given, so a
ledger row can never silently mis-join across stories — a mismatch is refused
before any host is spawned. Omitting `--reviewRunId` / `--lane` leaves
`threadId` / `subagentId` null (no empty-string pollution).

When `--storyId` is given **without** `--phase`, the phase is resolved through the
configured story store; a story unknown to that store is refused pre-spawn. When
`--phase` is supplied the store is never consulted, so `--phase` works with or
without `--storyId` even in a project whose story metadata lives under a
custom `storyDir`.

## Per-host usage semantics

Provider truth is preferred over estimates; an absence is recorded as an explicit
`source=unavailable`, never a fabricated zero.

- **codex** — parses the terminal `turn.completed` usage event from
  `codex exec --json` and maps it to `{ input: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens,
  cacheRead: cached_input_tokens, cacheCreation: null, output: output_tokens }`.
  The `input` field is the **uncached remainder** (codex `input_tokens` includes
  cached input); the original payload (including `reasoning_output_tokens`) is
  digested raw.
- **claude** — parses the stream-json `result` envelope usage via
  `parseClaudeCliOutput` (the four-field Anthropic usage plus the served model).
- **agy** — recorded as `source=unavailable` with provider `antigravity` and an
  explicit `unavailableReason`. agy print mode exposes no usage surface
  (verified 2026-07-10), so no counts can be reported.

A parse miss (no `turn.completed` event, no `result` usage) records an
`unavailable` final with a reason rather than inventing counts.

nothing"), and no second `unavailable` final is attempted for it.

non-zero exit — but the summary reports `recorded: none` with `recordId: null`

minted for a blocked row that never persisted.

## Caps (fail-closed, before spawn)

With the usage ledger enabled, both caps run at the choke point BEFORE a host
is spawned, and each refusal attempts to record a
`decision.kind=blocked` ledger row (diagnostics-honest; an append failure is
reported as `recorded: none`). With `LATTICE_USAGE_LEDGER=0`, budget enforcement
and every ledger row are disabled; the provider-process capacity admission
still runs before every spawn and refuses fail-closed without claiming a
blocked row was persisted.

- **Per-dispatch hard budget** — reuses the existing `LATTICE_HARD_BUDGET_TOKENS`
  preflight guard per call. An over-budget preflight estimate refuses with
  `reasonCode hard_budget_exceeded` before spawning.
- **Provider-process concurrency** — a shared slot registry under
  `.lattice/runtime/provider-process-slots/`

  live run (pid + `startedAt` + an acquire-minted **ownership token**).
  Admission and reclaim are serialized by the ownership-checked provider
  registry lock, then the selected fixed slot is created with exclusive `wx`.

  create one cross-process transaction, so simultaneous starts and corrupt-slot
  replacement cannot slip past the cap. When every index

  `<=0` falls back to the default; an explicit larger value is honored) is
  held, the run refuses fail-closed with a non-zero exit, prints the live-run
  list, and, when the ledger is enabled, writes a blocked row with `reasonCode
  concurrency_cap_exceeded`.
  Slot reclaim is **ownership-aware** (mirroring the ledger-lock doctrine
  below): a slot with a recorded **dead pid** is reclaimed at any age; a slot
  whose metadata is **missing/corrupt** (the holder crashed between creating
  the file and its metadata landing) is reclaimed once its mtime exceeds the
  `LATTICE_HOST_RUN_SLOT_STALE_MS` orphan backstop (default **6h**); a slot
  with a **live** recorded pid is **never reclaimed by age** — a long host run
  keeps its admission and waiters refuse at cap. Reclaim re-verifies the
  occupant immediately before the unlink under the same registry lock and then
  re-creates exclusively, so a crashed run never wedges the cap and a racing
  reclaimer cannot delete a slot a new holder just re-acquired. Slot release on
  exit is best-effort, registry-serialized and **token-guarded**:
  the file is unlinked only while it still carries the releasing run's own
  token, so a reclaimed-and-re-acquired slot survives the original holder's
  late release. Raising the cap mid-flight exposes more indexes; lowering it
  counts every live high-index slot and refuses new starts until the total live
  count drops below the new cap.

Proofbound launches Codex and Claude as managed cross-provider CLI processes.
`lattice host_run` submits those processes to a durable
`ManagedHostRun`: the detached worker, not the caller shell, owns the provider
until a terminal record exists. A caller may attach, time out, disconnect, or
return after 30 seconds without cancelling or replacing the provider run.

The same launch path records optional LLM usage diagnostics. Usage rows are not
the execution owner and disabling them does not disable shared provider-process
admission. `lattice usage_sweep` remains the read-only companion for sessions
that never used the managed boundary.

## Why this exists

A 2026-07-10 token-burn audit found the usage ledger only ever saw a handful of
probe rows: host-side reviewer launches, quorum cross-host reviews, and long
desktop sessions all burned real tokens that the ledger never recorded. Every
`host_run` receives a durable `runId`, an absolute deadline and an exclusive
terminal receipt. The runtime persists under the primary worktree at
`.lattice/runtime/host-runs/<runId>/`, so Story worktree cleanup cannot erase an
active run or its receipt; secrets and prompt bytes are 0600
one-shot inputs removed when the worker claims them. Interactive desktop and
native-subagent lifecycles remain outside this boundary and are covered only by
their host or by read-only retrospective diagnostics.

Usage rows are diagnostics only (`gateEvidence=false`). They never gate the
workflow, never satisfy REVIEW/TEST/DONE/Authority evidence, and never advance a
phase.

## `host_run`

```
lattice host_run --host <codex|claude> --agentType <type> \
  [--storyId B-xxxx] [--phase DEV] \
  ( --prompt "<text>" | --promptFile <path> ) \
  [--reviewRunId B-xxxx:RR-001] [--lane <reviewer-lane>] \
  [--timeoutMs <ms>] [--deadlineMs <ms>] [--detach] \
  [--json]
```

`--detach` returns after a bounded worker-claim handshake with
`runId/state/generation/deadlineAt`. Foreground mode submits the same durable
run and attaches to it; it does not own the provider child. Operators use:

```bash
lattice host_run_status '{"runId":"<runId>","afterGeneration":4,"afterSequence":12,"waitMs":30000,"json":true}'
lattice host_run_cancel '{"runId":"<runId>","reason":"operator cancelled"}'
```

`waitMs` is capped at 30 seconds. A bounded return means “wake the caller and
inspect the current snapshot”, not “the provider failed”. Completion is known
only from `state=completed|failed|cancelled|timed_out` plus the terminal
receipt. Provider-output silence and a stale output timestamp are diagnostics,
never terminal predicates and never automatic-restart authorization. The
absolute deadline prevents permanent waiting; the next status/cancel/attach
touch reconciles an overdue run to terminal truth and records whether process
cleanup made replacement safe.

The host subprocess executes in the **resolved project root** (the `--root`
target — the same root the usage-ledger rows are attributed to), independent of
the caller's current working directory, so where the host actually runs can
never diverge from where the ledger says it ran.

Provider output is durably journaled and projected to an attached foreground
caller as it arrives. Worker heartbeat and `lastProviderProgressAt` are separate:
the former proves only that the supervisor can update state; the latter moves
only when observable provider bytes arrive. `providerProgressMode=unobservable`
is reported honestly when progress cannot be observed. A one-line usage summary
is written to stderr, for example:

```
usage recorded: provider=openai input=10202 cacheRead=11008 output=85 (recordId llmuse_...)
```

Only a **bounded** amount of state is retained for usage parsing — the last
usage-bearing line (codex `turn.completed` / the claude `result` envelope),
capped at 1 MiB per line. A line over the cap is dropped (not retained), so a
flooding host can never exhaust memory or manufacture a count. Truncation
poisoning is tracked **relative to the retained usage candidate**: when a drop
happens **after** the retained usage line — or no usage line was ever
retained — the dropped line may have carried the real final numbers, so the
usage final records `unavailable` (reason `usage_line_retention_truncated`)
rather than a fabricated **or stale** value. A drop **followed by** a later
valid usage-bearing line does not poison the run: last-usage-wins makes the
later retained line the freshest usage information, so it is recorded honestly
(e.g. one huge non-usage output line early in the stream no longer discards a
perfectly good final usage event).

### Passthrough routing (text vs `--json`)

| Mode | Host stdout | Host stderr | Process stdout carries |
|---|---|---|---|
| text (default) | streamed live to **process.stdout** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | the live host stdout (the handler does not re-print it — no double-print) |
| `--json` | streamed live to **process.stderr** | streamed live to **process.stderr** | ONLY the single JSON result line (kept clean) |

In `--json` mode the full host transcript is delivered live on **stderr** so that
**stdout stays clean** for the one JSON result; the JSON `stdout` field therefore

contained into the same `passthroughError` state instead of crashing the process;
once a stream is known broken, the best-effort diagnostic writes to it are

outstanding writes are tracked with a shared pending counter (throughput is never
serialized) that the `finally` **drains before removing the listeners** — bounded
by a defensive ~2s cap so a pathologically wedged stream can never hang the
command — so a late EPIPE from the FINAL live stdout chunk of a text-mode run, or
from the FIRST stderr write of a quiet run (which never tripped the skip), still
fires while a listener is attached.

Exactly one of `--prompt` / `--promptFile` is required for ordinary managed
runs. Formal cross-provider reviewer mode is the exception: `--managedReview`
forbids both and derives the exact prompt from the signed ReviewRun. A host
non-zero exit (or a cap refusal) propagates as a non-zero process exit; in
`--json` mode `exitCode` is a field.

### Reviewer launch

Native direct `review_pass_set` / reviewer `finding_add` is formal evidence only
when the exact tool invocation carries a short-lived Ed25519 attestation from a
registered host-adapter broker. The signed claims bind the Story, agent and
lane, ReviewRun, writer session, signed dispatch prompt/binding, adapter and host
identity, and an invocation nonce. Lattice stores only the broker public-key
registration; it has no issuer command and does not keep the broker private key
in the repository or `.lattice` runtime state. The adapter injects the signed
attestation over a dedicated inherited descriptor for that exact Lattice CLI
process. Inline environment tokens are not accepted.

An adapter integration must therefore do both parts: register its public key in
`nativeReviewInvocation.brokers`, then sign and descriptor-inject each exact
review closeout invocation from its authenticated host tool-execution seam. If
the current Codex/Claude host does not provide that broker integration, native
direct evidence fails closed and is advisory-only; use the managed reviewer flow
below for formal evidence. `dispatch` and `review_run_start` do not issue this
capability, and a raw provider CLI cannot promote a self-generated key into the
registered broker set.

The attestation nonce is atomically consumed once to prevent replay. That local
ledger is replay protection, not a same-UID security boundary. Likewise process
ancestry is corroboration rather than required authority: an unavailable `ps`
view does not reject a valid broker attestation, but any observable mixed
Codex/Claude ancestry rejects direct evidence even when the nearest provider
matches. A same-UID/root attacker that can replace trusted configuration or
instrument the broker is outside this local assurance boundary.
